data.title: Browser Storage
data.tagline: Browser storage is a local web mechanism for keeping data in a person's current browser.
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether information only needs the current browser or must be stored by a backend and database for multiple devices or users.
data.description: It can remember dark mode, an unsubmitted form draft, or recently viewed projects so a later page load may restore them. It normally belongs only to that browser and device; clearing data, changing browser, or switching device may remove it.

learning.assumes: You have seen a site remember a theme, draft, or previous filter.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether information only needs the current browser or must be stored by a backend and database for multiple devices or users.

distinctions.label: Database
distinctions.explanation: Browser Storage usually stays in one person's current browser. A Database is managed by the backend and suits signed-in, shared, queryable, long-lived data.

explanation.title: Local preferences and short-lived work
explanation.text: Theme selection, an unfinished draft, and non-sensitive interface preferences can remain in the browser so a page quickly restores recent work.

explanation.title: Its scope is usually one browser
explanation.text: It does not automatically sync to another device or make the data available to another user. Important information must also account for data clearing, private mode, and capacity limits.

data.boundary: Browser storage is neither a server database nor a vault for secrets. A database supports server control, shared access, and more dependable persistence; information sent to a browser may be viewed or cleared by the person using that device.

lessonPractice.title: A team needs users to see the same submitted orders on both phone and computer. Where should the data primarily live?

options.label: In a server-controlled database, read through authenticated APIs; browser storage can only assist the local experience
options.feedback: Correct. Orders must work across devices and may need support staff or other systems, so the current browser cannot be the sole source.

options.label: Only in localStorage because it survives a refresh
options.feedback: Surviving a refresh does not synchronize devices or provide server-side authorization and reliable persistence.

options.label: Only in page state because the user does not need to leave this page
options.feedback: Page state commonly disappears after refresh or close and cannot represent a submitted order.

data.agentPrompt: Save the unsubmitted editing draft in browser storage and restore it after refresh; keep submitted content in the database through the API. Do not put secrets or authorization decisions in browser storage. Verify draft recovery after refresh and submitted content from another device.
